questions.text: Under NSCP Section 424.2.1, flexural members must have adequate stiffness to limit what?

options.text: Only reinforcement congestion.
Deflections or deformations that adversely affect strength or serviceability.
Only concrete temperature during curing.

rationale.correct: Section 424.2.1 requires adequate stiffness to limit deflections or deformations that adversely affect strength or serviceability.
rationale.takeaway: The checked anchor frames deflection as a serviceability and strength-protection check.

questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Table 9.5.1 (Ribbed Slab — Both Ends Continuous)

questions.text: A one-way solid slab with a 4 m simply supported span is initially designed at thickness = 200 mm per L/20 ratio. A code reviewer notes this is below minimum. What is the correct minimum thickness?

options.text: 200 mm (correct per L/20)
160 mm (thinner than specified, not meeting the minimum thickness required for structural integrity)
250 mm (per L/16, more conservative, ensuring compliance with additional safety margins)
The reviewer is wrong; 200 mm satisfies L/20.

questions.rationale: For a 4 m simply supported one-way solid slab, L/20 = 4000/20 = 200 mm exactly. The design is correct and meets NSCP Table 9.5.1. The reviewer's claim of non-compliance is incorrect; 200 mm IS the minimum (not 'below' it). [A]: 'a' correctly states 200 mm satisfies L/20; 'd' directly refutes the reviewer. [B]: 160 mm would be too thin and non-compliant. [C]: L/16 is not applicable to solid slabs; it is for ribbed beams.

questions.text: Unless a more comprehensive analysis is used, how is additional time-dependent deflection for non-prestressed flexural members treated?

options.text: As immediate sustained-load deflection multiplied by the Section 424 time-dependent factor expression.
As zero after shoring is removed.
As a fixed 10 mm allowance for every member.
As a fire-protection reduction factor.

rationale.correct: Section 424.2.4.1.1 calculates additional time-dependent deflection from creep and shrinkage as the immediate deflection caused by sustained load multiplied by the time-dependent factor expression.
rationale.takeaway: Time-dependent deflection is tied to sustained-load behavior.
